questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to extend behavior without touching core dispatch logic; demonstrates the Command pattern with a runtime registry.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern
- Registry-based extensibility
- Safe, non-invasive extension

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Command { execute(args: string[]): void; }
class Registry { private map = new Map<string, Command>(); register(name: string, c: Command) { this.map.set(name, c); } get(name: string): Command | undefined { return this.map.get(name); } }
class Router { constructor(private registry: Registry) {} route(argv: string[]) { const cmd = argv[0]; const command = this.registry.get(cmd); if (command) command.execute(argv.slice(1)); else throw new Error('Unknown command'); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle asynchronous commands? 
- How would you ensure thread-safety in a multi-process CLI?

## Why This Is Asked
Evaluates how a gateway can flexibly apply per-tenant policies without redeploys, testing runtime extensibility and concurrency-safe registries.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for interchangeable rate-limiters
- Registry for runtime policy discovery
- Lazy initialization and safe defaults
- Thread-safe caching in high-throughput paths

```javascript
interface IRateLimiter { acquire(tokens: number): Promise<boolean> }
class TokenBucketRateLimiter implements IRateLimiter { /* ... */ }
class FixedWindowRateLimiter implements IRateLimiter { /* ... */ }
class LeakyBucketRateLimiter implements IRateLimiter { /* ... */ }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test correctness under bursty traffic?
- How would you ensure memory usage stays bounded as tenants are added?

## Why This Is Asked
Explores designing an extensible rate limiter with runtime algorithm plug-ins for a high-scale gateway.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy + Registry for runtime extensibility
- Per-endpoint quotas and per-key isolation
- Clock abstraction for testability and skew handling

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Algorithm {
  shouldPass(key: string, now: number): boolean
  record(key: string, now: number): void
}
class Registry { register(name: string, factory: ()=>Algorithm): void; get(name:string): ()=>Algorithm }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you ensure thread-safety and lock-free reads for high throughput?
- How would you test time-based behavior and simulate clock skew?


- How would you handle rule dependencies and initialization order?
- How would you test hot-reload without affecting live traffic?

## Key Concepts
- Composite for hierarchical checks
- Registry for dynamic extension
- Lightweight HealthStatus aggregation

## Code Example
```javascript
interface IHealthCheck { name: string; check(): HealthStatus }
class SimpleCheck implements IHealthCheck { constructor(name, fn){...} check(){return new HealthStatus(...)}}
class CheckGroup implements IHealthCheck { constructor(name){this.children=[]} add(c){this.children.push(c)} check(){return aggregate(this.children)}}
```
